hints.func-mode: Neither the middle nor the biggest value answers this: the frequent one does.
hints.require-ref: Read the tickets from B2:B7 so a new ticket joins the answer on its own.
hints.value: Three tickets are size 3 and two are size 5, so the most common size is 3.
hints.error: #N/A says no size repeats. It describes the list, not a broken formula.

the largest value, 7, which appears only once
the first ticket is outside the range, so the counts are not the desk's

screens.prompt: Put the most common box count into C2, and notice it is not the middle of the list.

hints.syntax: MODE wants one range and nothing else: =MODE(B2:B8).
hints.func-mode: MODE counts repeats, so it can return 2 while the median of the same column sits at 4.
hints.require-ref: Read the stores from B2:B8 instead of listing the counts.
hints.value: Sorted, the seven counts run 2, 2, 2, 4, 7, 9 and 9: the median is 4 and the mode is 2.
hints.error: #VALUE! comes up only when a word is typed inside the brackets. Blank cells are skipped, so a half-filled column still answers.

reject.why: the middle value, 4, which occurs once
the first store is dropped, so the repeat count is wrong
triple the mode, 6, which no store ordered
division by zero, so the cell holds #DIV/0!
the closing bracket is missing, so nothing runs
one below the mode, 1, which no store ordered

docs.explain:
MODE looks for the value that occurs most often and gives back one of the values on the sheet, not a figure built from them. That makes it the summary for numbers that are really categories, such as shoe sizes and pack counts. Blank cells and text are skipped.

In the first grid, 3 appears three times and 5 twice, so the answer is 3. The second grid has 2 three times and 9 twice, so the answer is 2, while the median of that same column is 4.

Two values with the same count leave a choice. Classic MODE returns whichever appears first in the data, and MODE.MULT returns both, so decide which one the report means. COUNTIF supplies the count itself when the frequency belongs on the page.

errors.text: No value repeats, which leaves MODE nothing to return. A list of unique ticket sizes always lands here.
A word was passed as an argument in its own right, as in =MODE("S"), where a range would have ignored it.
Two sizes share the highest count, and MODE reports whichever it met first, so the number moves when the rows are reordered.

docs.atWork: A support desk sizing its ticket categories, and a warehouse stocking the box count each shop orders most often.
docs.outcome: Find the value that repeats most often, which is neither the biggest nor the middle.
docs.teaches: MODE, and how it differs from MEDIAN
docs.dataset: Support ticket sizes and box counts per store

seo.title: MODE in Excel: the most common value
seo.description: Mean and median sort by size, MODE by frequency, which suits shoe sizes and pack counts. A list where every value occurs once has no mode at all.
